question: Obtain Candid's full PCS code list (PCS_Taxonomy_Definitions_2024.xlsx, November 2024 release) through a channel its robots.txt and terms allow (the Taxonomy API with a key, or a copy supplied by Candid), then add a code-existence check to scripts/mission_validate_grant_record.py and code the Endaoment vector's education purpose
conclusion_affected: Whether schema v0.1 can check that a PCS code exists rather than only its shape; purpose coverage of the test vectors
rationale: The licence is CC BY 4.0 (read first-hand), but the xlsx sits under /content/*, which taxonomy.candid.org's robots.txt disallows, and the term-data host data.taxonomy.candid.org answers 401 for robots.txt; only four example codes (SC020000, PA020000, UA0000, TA00) could be read

question: Get Candid's NTEE-to-PCS crosswalk (the FAQ says 'You may request a copy by e-mailing') and test how many of the repo's Schedule I recipient NTEE codes map one-to-one, so recipient-level NTEE data can seed grant-level PCS codes
conclusion_affected: Feasibility of back-filling purpose codes from recipient classification; NTEE fallback path
rationale: PCS 'is based on the NTEE and the majority of the Subject codes overlap', but the crosswalk is available only on request (outreach, outside this pass). Endaoment already returns a recipient nteeCode (example E91)

question: Map the draft record to 360Giving 1.4 and back: write a converter for the three converted positive vectors and validate the output against the official 360Giving JSON schema (if its host's robots.txt allows the download), recording which fields are lost (fund_id, anonymity, status)
conclusion_affected: Whether an open DAF record can be published alongside 360Giving data without a parallel format
rationale: The schema map found 360Giving carries 5 of 8 core fields and no fund, donor-disclosure or status field; v0.1 uses US-EIN org-ids and a {vocabulary, code} purpose so the overlap is mechanical, but no round trip has been run

question: Cross-check the stdlib keyword-subset validator against a full JSON Schema 2020-12 implementation in an environment where installing one is allowed; all 24 vectors should give the same verdicts and the schema should pass the 2020-12 metaschema
conclusion_affected: Confidence that schema-v0.1.json behaves the same in third-party validators (if/then, oneOf on PCS facets)
rationale: This pass forbade package installs, so validation used a stdlib validator implementing 21 JSON Schema keywords (20 used by the schema) with a 12-case self-test; metaschema validation of the schema itself was not done

question: Endaoment grant lifecycle after asyncStatus: read the public OpenAPI for transfer-listing endpoints and document which field (if any) shows that a grant has been paid to the recipient, and whether Liquidated precedes or follows payment
conclusion_affected: Status mapping for Endaoment (pending / approved / paid); whether 'paid' can be filled from a public API at all
rationale: Endaoment's deprecated status (PendingReview/Approved/Rejected) no longer exposes approval and asyncStatus (PendingLiquidation/Liquidated/Cancelled) describes liquidation; the OpenAPI's own example value 'pending' is not in its enum. v0.1 maps only PendingLiquidation->pending and Cancelled->canceled

question: Sponsor grant letters and remittance advices: for the top-10 sponsors, record from public samples or help pages which of the record's fields a nonprofit actually receives (grant id, fund id or name, purpose text, anonymity level, payment reference), to test whether payment_reference and grant_id would close the remittance gap
conclusion_affected: Value of the payment_reference field; the remittance-matching problem in b4013-02
rationale: The wave-39A scope holds that no readable top-10 sponsor page states a grant ID in ACH addenda; Chariot requires its request id on 'the grant letter / remittance advice', so letters are where record fields already reach charities
